1: Welcome, syllabus, and a tour of this site. Choose your course level. Name-game icebreaker.
Read Ch. 1. Section 1.3: the sender–receiver (transactional) model. Watch a communication-model video, then label the diagram: sender, receiver, message, channel, noise, feedback, context.
Model in action: back-to-back drawing. One partner describes a picture, the other draws it, first with no feedback, then with questions allowed. Name the noise you noticed.
Section 1.2: why nerves are normal; watch a speech-anxiety video. Introduce the Self-Introduction Speech and its rubric; choose your object.
Section 1.2: why nerves are normal; watch a speech-anxiety video. Introduce the Personal Artifact Speech and its rubric; choose your artifact.
Vocabulary check on the communication process. Delivery basics: eye contact, voice, posture. Partner practice.

Work day: finish slides and your note card. Rehearse with a partner.
Work day: finish slides. Key-word speaking outline due.
SPEECH Finish speeches. Reflection: one strength and one goal.

Listening and peer feedback norms. Practice giving feedback on an example video.
Read Ch. 4. Choosing a topic. Brainstorm and sign up for your Heritage Month person (no repeats in a class).
Credible versus weak sources: sorting activity.
Gale orientation: logging in and searching for your person.

Read Ch. 5. Gale deep dive: the Peer-Reviewed filter, reading a scholarly article, and the Cite tool.
APA 7 references. Practice with MyBib and Gale’s Cite tool.
Oral citations: saying a source out loud with its credentials.
Research work day. Source check with the teacher.
Research work day. Annotated bibliography check with the teacher.

Read Ch. 7. Using evidence: facts, examples, and testimony.

Read Ch. 8. Introductions, conclusions, and transitions. Draft your hook.
Build slides: Early Life & Roots, Achievements.
Storytelling: watch “The Magical Science of Storytelling” and add a story to each main point.

Work day: References slides. Preparation outline due.
Peer rehearsal round 1 with a timer.
Final rehearsal. Academic Integrity slide check.
8: Reflection and peer feedback. Celebrate the people we learned about.

Read Ch. 10. Clear, concrete language and signposts.
Choose a process. Review prop rules. Plan your steps.
Build slides and take your step photos.

Full rehearsal with props and a timer. Preparation outline due.

Choose your story in the Story Builder. Your story, your choice: pick one you are comfortable sharing.
Map your story arc: hook, setting, build-up, turning point, after, lesson.
Bring it to life: vivid details, show don’t tell. Tell your story to a partner.
Make your key-word card. Rehearse with a timer (3–5 minutes).

Browse Britannica ProCon and choose your question.
Monroe’s Motivated Sequence. Watch the annotated example.
Write your thesis and plan three arguments.
Choose a community problem and the decision-maker who can fix it.
Research work day. Plan your local source or interview.

Fallacy hunt: find weak reasoning in ads and posts.
Build slides: attention, need, and satisfaction.
15: Visualization and action: your specific ask (who, what, by when).
